title: Plus One
prompt: You are given a large integer represented as an integer array `digits`, where each `digits[i]` is the `i`th digit of the integer from most significant to least significant, with no leading zeroes. Increment the large integer by one and return the resulting array of digits.

examples.explanation: 99 + 1 = 100, which needs an extra leading digit.

constraints: digits does not contain leading zeroes (other than possibly a single zero itself)
hints: Converting the whole array to an integer, adding one, and converting back works but feels like cheating the digit-array representation — and can be unsafe for arbitrarily long numbers in other languages.
Adding one only cascades a carry through a suffix of 9s; everything before the first non-9 digit (from the right) is untouched.
Scan from the last digit backward: if it's less than 9, just increment it and return immediately; if it's 9, set it to 0 and continue the carry leftward. If the carry runs off the front, prepend a 1.

solution.approach: Walk the digits from right to left, simulating grade-school addition. If the current digit is less than 9, incrementing it absorbs the carry completely, so it can be returned immediately. If it's 9, it rolls over to 0 and the carry continues to the next digit left. If the carry propagates past the leftmost digit (the whole number was all 9s), prepend a 1 to represent the extra digit. This touches only the trailing run of 9s plus one digit, never needing a full numeric conversion.
